summary: Lolo National Forest lookout nine miles southwest of Seeley Lake; a 30-ft pole L-4 tower from 1932, listed destroyed in 1957 or removed. No source describes the site today.

facts.status_note: Gone. One listing says destroyed in 1957; another says removed, with no date.

events.note: Dale White reported as the Forest Service lookout atop Belmont Peak, August 1937 (Billings Gazette, quoted by Forest Lookouts)

evidence.supports: built 1932 as a 30-foot pole L-4 tower; destroyed 1957
about nine miles southwest of Seeley Lake
Dale White, 24-year-old Forest Service lookout atop Belmont Peak, 1937
evidence.quote: Dale White of Missoula, 24-year-old forest service lookout whose station is atop Belmont peak in the Lolo forest

evidence.supports: White reported he was cut across the face with a knife
evidence.quote: reported he was slashed across the face with a knife

evidence.supports: the encounter was an attempted arrest for a game violation
evidence.quote: when he attempted to make an arrest

evidence.supports: Forest Lookouts marks the site removed, no date
association list shows the tower as gone
the White report is dated August 13, 1937
the report is from the Billings Gazette
the man was a game law violator
evidence.quote: by an Indian game law violator

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Firelookout.com says destroyed in 1957; Forest Lookouts says removed, with no date. Both agree the tower is gone, and the story gives both accounts.

notes_for_editor: Thin: two listing pages and one 1937 newspaper item quoted on the Forest Lookouts page. No description of the site today was found. Firelookout.com credits 'Lolo National Forest/Montana DNRC'; the record names only the Forest Service. The 1937 injury is reported as White's own account, in the story's words.
